result.document_summary: Part 1 of Chapter 155 (Rent Control) of the Hoboken, NJ municipal code, covering definitions, exemptions, base-rent control, the annual cost-of-living cap, surcharges, hardship increases and administration.
result.notes: Part 1 of 2; the text ends mid-section (155-23), so later provisions, including vacancy decontrol, registration and condo/co-op owner-occupant provisions, are not in this part. Chapter 155 is the only rule instrument extracted; its surcharges, hardship increases, exemptions and refund periods are recorded as details of that one record. Just-cause eviction is only referenced through a definition pointing to N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53, which does not state the rule itself, so no just-cause record was output. The chapter was adopted in 1984 (Ord. C329), with the base rent date of October 1, 1985; the effective date of the original ordinance is not stated in the document, so none was given.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control: base-rent control and annual increase cap
rules.requirement: Rents in covered dwellings are controlled at the base rent received on October 1, 1985. At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not raise rent by more than the lesser of 5% or the CPI change. Only one cost-of-living increase is permitted in any twelve-month period, increases require 30 days' written notice, and increases beyond those allowed are void and refundable. Separate board-approved surcharges (taxes, water/sewer, capital improvements) and hardship increases are also available.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI change; one increase per 12 months
rules.citation: Hoboken City Code ch. 155, § 155-5 (Ord. No. B-532)
rules.quoted_span: no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units (buildings or structures rented or offered for rent to one or more tenants) in Hoboken, other than the listed exemptions.

exemptions.label: Newly constructed dwellings on first rental

all_of.value: newly constructed dwelling, first rental only, registered with the Rent Regulation Officer
all_of.text: Newly constructed dwellings which are rented for the first time (exempt only for the initial rent or lease agreement, if registered before first rental).
Nonresidential and commercial property (commercial units in a mixed building are exempt; apartment units remain covered).

exemptions.label: Student housing owned or controlled by a school

all_of.value: student housing provided by a school, college or similar institution that owns or controls it
all_of.text: Housing provided for students by a school, college or similar institution which owns or controls that housing.

all_of.value: housing owned and operated by state or federal government agencies
all_of.text: Housing owned and operated by other government agencies, such as the state or federal government.

all_of.value: building completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984, not vacated through unlawful means, registered before renting (exempt on first rental only)
all_of.text: A building completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984, provided it did not become vacant through unlawful means and is registered before renting.

all_of.value: landlord complied with N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 notice requirements; exemption lasts the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after construction (30 years if no initial mortgage)
all_of.text: Exemption applies only where the landlord complied with N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq. and only for the period stated in the ordinance.

exemptions.label: Housing under preempting governmental agency rent regulation

all_of.value: landlord contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent and supersedes city authority
all_of.text: Chapter is preempted during the period of governmental agency rent regulation under a contract that supersedes city authority.

rules.exemptions_text: Exempt: motels/hotels; first rental of newly constructed dwellings; industrial and commercial property; school-controlled student housing; government-owned housing; buildings vacant since 1/1/1984 (first rental only); multiple dwellings built after 6/25/1987 for a limited period under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1; units under preempting government-agency rent regulation during that period.
rules.interaction: Exemption for post-1987 multiple dwellings applies in accordance with N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq. The chapter is preempted while a governmental agency's rent regulation superseding the City's authority is in effect.
yields_to: Rent regulation by a preempting governmental agency under contract
